Review PR #337 in software-mansion/argent. Use the `gh` CLI to fetch it.

Before doing anything else, fetch this PR and find out WHO AUTHORED IT: `gh pr view 337 --repo software-mansion/argent --json author,isDraft,headRefName`. Everything below depends on the answer — handle the PR as exactly ONE of the two cases that follow, never both.

Identify the behavior this PR sets out to change from its description, the relevant issue and the code, and judge its premise: whether the diagnosis holds and the change removes the cause rather than hiding the symptom. A finding must show a reachable regression against the merge base of the PR’s target branch, a supported case where the submitted head fails a behavior the change explicitly promises, or a workaround that leaves in place a cause this repo could fix. Give the trigger, the expected or base result, the head result and the changed line responsible. Compare the same input on both revisions when the baseline is uncertain. A partial fix can satisfy its stated scope. An adjacent defect already present on the base, a preferred design and wording without a behavioral consequence do not qualify. Keep incidental pre-existing defects in the private summary only. Open a follow-up issue only when the operator explicitly asks.

For each PR, dispatch swarms of agents across the review moves — claims vs code (every comment, docstring, description, error message, type, test name and README line the change touches or silently falsifies still tells the truth about the code), nearest twin (each changed rule, constant, guard, mapping or message agrees with whatever does the same job elsewhere: the other platform, the other call site, the other arm of the same branch), non-happy paths (errors, timeouts, cancellation, partial success and missing input: what the caller is told, what state is left behind, and above all whether anything reports success for work it did not do), inputs (empty, non-finite, boundary, misspelled or extra keys, alternate spellings, and shapes only one platform produces, including the message each one gets), reachability both ways (whether each branch or guard can actually fire or is shadowed by an earlier check, and whether its value reaches the consumer it was written for), and what outlives the call (processes, temp files, caches, device state, two callers racing one file, and every timeout on the path summed against the budget the code claims) — plus the absence pass, which finds what is missing by comparing against a reference: a sibling that has it, prose that promises it, symmetry (spawn/reap, open/close, write/delete, set/reset), and, when coverage of the central behavior is in doubt, a targeted mutation that reverts that behavior. For every suspected HIGH / MEDIUM issue, build a concrete, hard reproduction that proves it real BEFORE touching anything. Maximum rigor. For each PR: run it END-TO-END through its real entry point and confirm observable behaviour — not just that it compiles.

Verify findings at the selected depth. Spend runtime verification on credible behavioral consequences and rerun the original reproduction before reporting a fix. Size any swarm to the work, with at most eight agents running at once. When a subagent's summary is spilled to a file, open it at the EXACT path that delegation handed back and never by globbing or listing the summary cache: several reviews run at once on this machine against one shared agent home, and those filenames carry a task index and a timestamp but nothing that names their owner, so a pattern match quietly returns a sibling review's findings for a different PR.

Diplomat attribution tag — a REQUIRED exception to the no-attribution rule, for GitHub commentary only: every comment, inline review comment, review body, and review-thread reply you post as part of this task must begin with the exact prefix `\[[Diplomat](https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat)\]: `, copied character for character — the `\[` and `\]` are literal brackets, only the word Diplomat is a Markdown link (to https://github.com/latekvo/Diplomat), anything after that link is plain text, and a colon and a space close it — followed by the text you would otherwise have written, so it renders as "[Diplomat]: <your text>".

▸ CASE A — @testuser authored this PR (it's MINE). Do everything in this case:

Keep dispatching swarms until every PR you go through comes back clean — where CLEAN means a pass that surfaced no HIGH and no MEDIUM finding. A pass whose findings are all LOW (or nitpicks) COUNTS AS CLEAN: drop the nitpicks and stop iterating on that PR.

If a PR turns out perfectly clean — no issues, regressions or bad practices left at ANY level — mark it ready for review. List every PR you cleared at the end.

For review threads that OTHERS have left on these PRs: address each one.

On my own PR, a finding is never posted — not as an inline comment, a review, or a top-level comment — it is FIXED on the branch and pushed. This includes LOW findings that meet the review scope. Treat every finding an earlier Diplomat run already posted on the PR under my own login (a comment opening with the Diplomat tag) exactly like a reviewer's: fix it or dismiss it with a reason, then resolve its thread. Reply "Fixed in <commit_hash>" or the reason on every finding thread you fix or dismiss, and never resolve one before that reply.

No AI attribution anywhere in git/GitHub — commits authored as me, no Co-Authored-By, no "Generated with" taglines.

▸ CASE B — someone OTHER than @testuser authored this PR (it's THEIRS). Do everything in this case instead:

These PRs are SOMEONE ELSE'S — UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES may you commit, push, or otherwise modify their branch. Your one and only deliverable is the code review itself. On a first review use the merge-base-to-head diff. On re-review find the most recent submitted, non-dismissed review bearing the Diplomat tag from this account on this PR and its reviewed commit. If that commit is an ancestor of the current head and the PR still targets the same branch, review only the intervening PR changes, their affected callers and unresolved findings. Exclude changes brought in solely from the target branch. On the same head check outstanding threads only. If the reviewed commit is unavailable, history was rewritten, or the target changed, use the full current PR diff. Apply the chosen depth within that range.

Anything you post on someone else's PR goes in ONE formal GitHub review, built through GitHub's review lifecycle: open it pending, put every comment inside it, then submit it. Never post on the PR through a top-level comment, nor through the standalone `pulls/<number>/comments` endpoint, which publishes every comment as a separate review of its own. (0) CHECK, first, before any review work: list the PR's reviews (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews`) and read the comments of any PENDING one of mine (`.../reviews/<id>/comments`). If one of them does not open with the `\[[Diplomat](` attribution tag (whatever model name follows it), that review is my own draft from the browser: stop right there — post nothing, and say so in your summary. One whose comments all carry the tag, or that has none, was left by an earlier run: you reuse or replace it at (1), and if you end without opening a review, delete it. (1) OPEN, only once your findings are final, right before you fill it: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews -f commit_id=<head sha>` with NO `event` field leaves the review PENDING, visible to nobody but me. GitHub allows one pending review per person per PR, so if that call is refused because one already exists, list the PR's reviews and read the PENDING one's comments. If it has no comments, or every comment opens with the attribution tag, it is yours — opened earlier in this run, or left by an earlier one. If its `commit_id` is the PR's current head, keep using it, after deleting any of its comments this run is not to post; otherwise delete it (`gh api -X DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>`) and open a fresh one. Otherwise it is my own draft, begun while you worked: stop as in (0). (2) FILL: add each comment anchored to its exact line(s) with the GraphQL `addPullRequestReviewThread` mutation (`pullRequestReviewId` = the pending review's `node_id`; `path`, `line`, `side`, plus `startLine` for a range), and each reply on an existing thread with `addPullRequestReviewThreadReply` carrying the same `pullRequestReviewId`, so it lands inside this review too. (3) SUBMIT, once, after the last comment is in — and right before it, list the pending review's comments again: one that does not open with the attribution tag is mine, added from the browser, so leave the review unsubmitted and stop as in (0). Otherwise: `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>/events -f event=COMMENT -f body=<what you checked, the result, and any optional coverage note allowed below>` — COMMENT unless a verdict instruction below explicitly tells you to APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES; such a verdict is this same submission's event, never a second review. Never end your turn with the review still PENDING: its comments reach no one until it is submitted. If you end with no inline comment, thread reply or optional body note to post and no instruction below to submit a review anyway, delete it instead (`gh api -X DELETE repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<number>/reviews/<id>`). Neither rule touches a draft of mine: after a stop, never submit, fill, or delete it.

Post your findings in that review. Put each distinct, verified behavioral finding on its changed line and explain the trigger and impact. Leave the choice of fix to the author. Label it Blocking when the consequence warrants holding the merge, for example when the change disables an existing workflow entirely on a supported runtime. Label smaller verified defects Non-blocking. Read existing threads from every reviewer first, including resolved threads. Keep one thread per defect. For an unresolved thread, retry the original trigger on the current head. Once that trigger passes, the finding is fixed. Never extend its acceptance criteria with a different input or mutant. A new defect in the intervening changes must independently pass the scope test. Reply on the original thread only when a claimed fix still fails its original trigger or you have new evidence relevant to the discussion. Respect a reasoned deferral. Leave resolved threads alone.

A surviving mutant alone shows a coverage gap. When reverting the PR’s central behavior leaves its tests green, you may include one short Optional coverage note in the review body. Combine related gaps there. A coverage note earns no inline thread, holds up no verdict and requires no further pass. Drop incidental test gaps.

Do NOT mark this PR ready for review and do NOT change its draft/ready state in any way.

When there are no in-scope behavioral findings, submit a COMMENT review with a short body saying what you actually checked and thanking the author (“Thank you for contributing”).
